★★★ THE RUNNABLE WITNESS FOR D-ASM-X86-IMMEDIATE-WINDOW-REFUSES-WHAT-GAS-TRUNCATES, closed in cycle P34 on an OPERATOR RULING.

★★★ WHY IT IS A CORPUS EXAMPLE AND NOT ONLY A UNIT PIN. Two separate facts have to hold and the unit tier can only see one of them cheaply. (1) THE FILE MUST ASSEMBLE — before P34 both `movw` spellings were refused with `A_ImmediateOperandOutOfRange`, so this example could not have existed; its mere presence in a green corpus is the conformance half. (2) THE EMITTED BITS MUST BE THE REFERENCE'S BITS — and a wrong narrowing still assembles, still links and still loads. Only an exit code that DEPENDS on the narrowed value separates 'it compiled' from 'it compiled correctly', which is the same reason the negative-scalar example beside this one exists.

★★ WHAT EACH HALF PINS.
  • HALF 1 is the case GNU as 2.42 DOES mention: ✔MEASURED `mov $0x1BEEF, %cx` → rc=0, `66 b9 ef be`, "Warning: 0x1beef shortened to 0xbeef". DSS emits the same immediate and warns too.
  • HALF 2 is THE CASE THE RULING EXISTS FOR: ✔MEASURED `mov $-32769, %cx` → rc=0, `66 b9 ff 7f`, and **NO DIAGNOSTIC AT ALL**. 0x8000 of magnitude vanishes with nothing on the reference's stderr. Matching gas EXACTLY would have imported that silence along with the bytes; the third arm takes the ACCEPTANCE from the reference and the LOUDNESS from the old refusal, because the disjunction rule constrains what DSS must COMPILE, never what it must stay QUIET about.

★ EACH HALF COMPARES THE NARROWED SPELLING AGAINST THE IN-WINDOW SPELLING OF THE SAME 16 BITS rather than against a literal. A hard-coded expected constant would pass if the encoder and the test drifted together; `movw $0x1BEEF, %cx` vs `movw $0xBEEF, %dx` cannot drift together, because the second spelling is inside the silence window and takes a different code path to the same field.

★ THE FOUR OUTCOMES ARE ALL DISTINCT — 42 correct · 52 positive half wrong · 142 negative half wrong · 152 both — so a partial regression cannot be read as a partial pass. The magnitudes differ (10 vs 100) for exactly that reason.

★ THIS EXAMPLE COMPILES WITH WARNINGS BY DESIGN, WHICH IS THE POINT AND NOT AN OVERSIGHT. Two `A_ImmediateNarrowedToOperandField` warnings are emitted, one per half, and the runner's gate is `errorCount() == 0` rather than a zero-diagnostic gate — so a green run here states BOTH that the narrowing is accepted AND that it is not silent. ⚠ If a future change made the narrowing suppressible or demoted it out of the stream, this example would still be green; that half is pinned in `tests/asm/test_asm_x86_width_and_direction.cpp` (`NarrowingDiagnosticIsUnsuppressable`), which is where the suppression claim belongs.

★ ONLY REGISTERS VOLATILE UNDER *BOTH* ABIs ARE TOUCHED — rax, rcx, rdx — so the same file is correct on System V and on Win64. The frame is hand-written (`subq $64, %rsp` / `addq $64, %rsp`) because that is what the `encode` tier means: no `materializeCallingConvention` runs here, and 64 keeps %rsp 16-byte aligned.

★ THE `release` ARM, SCOPED HONESTLY. At the `encode` tier no MIR module exists, so the optimizer, the register allocator and calling-convention materialization never run — this arm does NOT witness the optimizer and cannot. It pins the narrower fact that `--config=release` still produces a working binary from assembly text, and that naming a pipeline does not BREAK an assembly example.

No pipeline can transform it and no edit to this example could ever make this arm differ, so the arm's exit-code comparison is x==x where the image is identical. HONEST BY CONSTRUCTION and deliberately NOT given "mustDifferFromBaseline" — an honest no-op, not a missed opt-in. Same scoping as the sibling asm_x86_64_negative_immediate_and_displacement example.
